svg.aria-label: Eight radar charts, one per upscaler, each with 10 spokes; on every spoke the best of the eight reaches the outer ring and the others reach in proportion to it, so a larger shape is better and a dent is a weakness. This project's 4.1.2l-lossy DLL comes first, and its shape is the dashed outline in the other seven. Still picture and moving background, mean: accuracy (dB): FSR 4.1.1 47.58 dB, Lossy 46.69 dB, 4.1.2l-lossy 46.84 dB, FSR 4.1.2 Lite 47.03 dB, FSR 3.1 45.02 dB, HLX FSR 4 47.26 dB, HelixSR 2.0 / HLX DLSS 45.27 dB, XeSS 45.54 dB. Thin railing in motion: accuracy (dB): FSR 4.1.1 41.61 dB, Lossy 40.58 dB, 4.1.2l-lossy 40.53 dB, FSR 4.1.2 Lite 40.95 dB, FSR 3.1 38.95 dB, HLX FSR 4 40.94 dB, HelixSR 2.0 / HLX DLSS 39.86 dB, XeSS 39.56 dB. Areas a moving object has just uncovered, mean of a panning and a still camera: accuracy (dB): FSR 4.1.1 32.91 dB, Lossy 34.61 dB, 4.1.2l-lossy 32.34 dB, FSR 4.1.2 Lite 33.52 dB, FSR 3.1 30.25 dB, HLX FSR 4 33.37 dB, HelixSR 2.0 / HLX DLSS 29.63 dB, XeSS 32.31 dB. Old image beside a moving object, mean of seven scenes: error (of 255): FSR 4.1.1 1.92, Lossy 2.30, 4.1.2l-lossy 2.36, FSR 4.1.2 Lite 2.52, FSR 3.1 3.20, HLX FSR 4 2.58, HelixSR 2.0 / HLX DLSS 3.63, XeSS 4.84. Thin bars fixed on screen in front of a panning background, mean of four pans: error where their old image lands (of 255): FSR 4.1.1 0.82, Lossy 0.91, 4.1.2l-lossy 0.85, FSR 4.1.2 Lite 1.28, FSR 3.1 1.04, HLX FSR 4 1.29, HelixSR 2.0 / HLX DLSS 2.98, XeSS 3.85. Tiny fast sparks: share of their brightness shown (%): FSR 4.1.1 83%, Lossy 72%, 4.1.2l-lossy 75%, FSR 4.1.2 Lite 76%, FSR 3.1 40%, HLX FSR 4 75%, HelixSR 2.0 / HLX DLSS 79%, XeSS 50%. Leaves swaying without motion vectors, mean of three sway speeds: error (of 255): FSR 4.1.1 11.0, Lossy 12.2, 4.1.2l-lossy 12.3, FSR 4.1.2 Lite 10.0, FSR 3.1 16.7, HLX FSR 4 10.0, HelixSR 2.0 / HLX DLSS 14.2, XeSS 14.3. Still picture: change per frame (of 255): FSR 4.1.1 0.037, Lossy 0.023, 4.1.2l-lossy 0.026, FSR 4.1.2 Lite 0.029, FSR 3.1 0.014, HLX FSR 4 0.024, HelixSR 2.0 / HLX DLSS 0.022, XeSS 0.084. Thin wire under a slow pan: how close its brightness is to the true one (%): FSR 4.1.1 90.5%, Lossy 71.0%, 4.1.2l-lossy 55.3%, FSR 4.1.2 Lite 62.1%, FSR 3.1 90.2%, HLX FSR 4 62.2%, HelixSR 2.0 / HLX DLSS 79.7%, XeSS 81.0%. Time per upscale call, mean of 1080p, 1440p and 4K output (ms): FSR 4.1.1 2.70 ms, Lossy 1.33 ms, 4.1.2l-lossy 1.02 ms, FSR 4.1.2 Lite 1.23 ms, FSR 3.1 0.73 ms, HLX FSR 4 1.23 ms, HelixSR 2.0 / HLX DLSS 1.24 ms, XeSS 2.88 ms.
svg.text: The shape of each upscaler: 10 measures
On every spoke the best of the eight reaches the outer ring. Bigger is better; a dent is a weakness. Dashed: the 4.1.2l-lossy DLL.
old image of things fixed on screen
brightness close to the true one
A spoke at half length: twice the error (or the change per frame, or the time) of the best of the eight; for sparks, half as much shown.
Orange: this project's lossy and 4.1.2l-lossy DLLs (frame skipping, they change the picture). FSR 4.1.2 Lite: AMD's small model, run in this
project's local test harness. HelixSR 2.0 / HLX DLSS: the same picture. Test rig, 4K output, one card, single runs.
